You are Koda building **Sprint 10 — Mobile + Touch Polish**. Also fold in the 6 Sprint 8 BLOCKERS (Sage FAILED S8 at 84.25/100).

## Project
Root: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`

## Inputs (MUST READ)
1. `.handoffs/sprint-8-blockers-queue.md` — **CRITICAL, fix FIRST (6 blockers, ~2h total)**
2. `.handoffs/sage-sprint-8-review.md` — full review context
3. `.handoffs/vega-sprint-10-spec.md` — Sprint 10 contract

6. `~/.claude/plans/giggly-kindling-bee.md` Sprint 10
7. `CLAUDE.md` + `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

## PART A — Sprint 8 Critical Blockers (DO FIRST)

**C1** — `app/api/clients/route.ts:22-25` — accept `last_visit_range` as enum key (`7d|30d|90d|all`). Map to ISO range in the route before query.

**C2** — `components/guest-artists/GuestEngagementTabs.tsx:31-33` — Guest Access UI/API/DB three-way name mismatch. Pick DB column names as source of truth. Rename UI + API payload to match. Verify PATCH actually updates DB columns.

**C3, C4, C5** — Schedule grid Actions dropdown field-name mismatches on three routes:
- `POST /api/schedule/copy-week` (C3)
- `POST /api/schedule/apply-template` (C4)
- `POST /api/schedule/templates` (C5)
Align request body field names between UI (`app/(app)/artists/schedules/page.tsx:237-294`) and API validator. Pick one convention and stick.

**C6** — `components/settings/team/PermissionsMatrix.tsx:306-307` — React Fragment missing `key` in map. Use `<React.Fragment key={id}>` or extract into a component.

Commit 1: `fix(sprint-8-blockers): C1-C6 field-name alignment + Fragment key warning`

Verify: `rm -rf .next && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint --max-warnings=0 && pnpm build` — must pass cold.

## PART B — Sprint 10 per Vega spec

### B1 — MobileNav (`components/shared/MobileNav.tsx`)
- Hamburger trigger in AppHeader, only below md
- Sheet side="left"
- User section at top (avatar + name + studio)
- Nav groups mirror sidebar (reuse filtered navGroups from AppLayout — no duplicate logic)
- Sign out at bottom
- Auto-close on nav

### B2 — CommandPalette mobile → BottomSheet
Below md, render CommandPalette inside existing BottomSheet. Use `useIsMobile()` hook (create if missing). Inner Command content identical on both paths.

### B3 — DataTable mobile stacked cards
Vega spec says partial exists. Add `mobileCardRender?: (row) => ReactNode` prop for per-table customization. Apply to: clients, appointments, artists, payments, commissions, inventory, audit log, payroll runs.

### B4 — BottomSheet rollout
Create `<ResponsiveDialog>` wrapper. Replaces Dialog with BottomSheet on mobile for: new appointment quick-add, photo lightbox options, settings per-section editors, confirm destructive, team member action menu.

### B5 — Touch targets audit
Every Button size="icon" / IconButton / MenuItem — 44×44 minimum hit area.
- `NumberInput` step buttons: `h-11 w-11 md:h-5 md:w-8`
- Calendar view toggle buttons
- DataTable row action menus

### B6 — PullToRefresh (`components/shared/PullToRefresh.tsx`)
Native PointerEvent, 80px threshold, spinner states ("Pull"/"Release"/"Refreshing…"). Apply to: `/appointments`, `/clients`, `/payments`, `/commissions`, `/payroll`.

### B7 — Responsive typography
Body `text-[13px] md:text-sm`. Headings scale down 2 steps on mobile. Tabular-nums for money.

### B8 — Safe-area utilities
`.safe-bottom { padding-bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }`. Apply to FABs, bottom sheets, sticky bottom CTA bars. Add `viewport: { viewportFit: 'cover' }` to root layout metadata.

### B9 — Mobile tabs
Scrollable row below md with fade-edge gradient. Underline style. Current tab scrolls into view on mount.

### B10 — Mobile empty states
EmptyState `compact?: boolean` prop (auto-applied below md). Shorter copy, larger icons (~64px), single CTA.

### B11 — Keyboard avoidance
`useKeyboardAware()` hook using `visualViewport` API. Scroll active input into view when keyboard opens.

### B12 — Mobile bottom nav
Per Nova: 5-slot bottom nav (Calendar / Clients / New / Inventory / More). `md:hidden`. FAB replaced by the center "New" slot.

### B13 — `/dev/design` Mobile section (18)
MobileNav preview, BottomSheet demo, stacked DataTable preview, PullToRefresh demo, safe-area visualizer.

## Hard rules
- Base-ui `render={<X/>}` pattern
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` conditional spread
- No raw hex / default shadows / **no `any`** / no `console.*`
- Sprint 9 lesson: avoid `(supabase as any)` — use proper TS types
- Use all prior components

## Acceptance
```bash
rm -rf .next && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint --max-warnings=0 && pnpm build
```
All clean cold-cache. Plus:
- No horizontal scroll on any page at 375px
- All interactive elements ≥ 44×44 hit area
- Safe-area respected on FABs + bottom sheets + CTA bars
- Bottom nav visible only below md

## Commits (10-12)
1. `fix(sprint-8-blockers): C1-C6 field alignment + Fragment key`
2. `feat(mobile): MobileNav + hamburger in AppHeader below md`
3. `feat(mobile): CommandPalette BottomSheet + useIsMobile hook`
4. `feat(mobile): DataTable mobileCardRender + stacked cards rollout`
5. `feat(mobile): ResponsiveDialog + BottomSheet rollout`
6. `fix(a11y): 44×44 touch targets — NumberInput + view toggle + row actions`
7. `feat(mobile): PullToRefresh + 5 list routes`
8. `feat(mobile): responsive typography + safe-area utilities + viewport fit`
9. `feat(mobile): scrollable fade-edge tabs + mobile empty state variant + keyboard aware hook`
10. `feat(mobile): bottom nav 5-slot with center-new FAB replacement`
11. `feat(dev): /dev/design Mobile section 18`

Each commit: typecheck + lint clean cold-cache.
Close note to `.handoffs/inkos-sprint-10-lessons.md`. 200-word return summary.

9	## 1. Bottom navigation vs hamburger
10	
11	**Winners use bottom nav, period.** Linear rebuilt mobile in Oct 2025 around a customizable bottom toolbar — users can pin the 4–5 features they hit daily (Pulse, My Issues, Inbox, projects). Fresha business, Cron iOS, and Height all ship bottom tab bars. Stripe Dashboard uses bottom tabs in native app but falls back to hamburger on mobile-web — the weakest pattern of the six. Notion mobile-web uses a top-left hamburger and is widely complained about on reddit.
12	
13	**InkOS verdict:** Bottom nav with 5 slots on `md:` breakpoint. Slots: **Calendar · Clients · New (FAB-slot) · Inventory · More**. Everything else under "More" as a sheet. Hide bottom nav on focused flows (booking wizard, consent form) to kill thumb distraction. Hamburger never.

15	## 2. Mobile data tables → stacked cards
16	
17	Below `md:` (768px) every table collapses to a vertical card list. Linear's issue list is the gold standard: **title (16/600) on line 1, status dot + assignee avatar + due chip on line 2, priority + project on line 3**. Stripe payments on mobile-web stacks amount + status on line 1, customer + date on line 2, chevron right. Fresha's client list: avatar · name+phone · last visit date.
18	
19	**Card anatomy for InkOS (375×~88px tap row):**
20	- Line 1: primary (client name / booking title) — 16px/600, truncate
21	- Line 2: 2–3 chips (status · artist · time) — 12px/500
22	- Line 3: metadata (service · price) — 12px/400 muted
23	- Whole card tappable, `min-h-[64px]`, `active:bg-muted`, chevron optional
24	
25	Never horizontal-scroll a desktop table on mobile. Reports page = tabs → cards, not scroll.
26	
27	## 3. Bottom sheets replace dialogs
28	
29	**Rule:** on `<md`, every `<Dialog>` becomes a bottom sheet. Native research shows bottom sheets get 25–30% higher engagement than centered modals because they match thumb position and dismiss with a natural swipe-down.
30	
31	Use Vaul (React drawer) with:
32	- **Snap points:** `[0.4, 0.9]` — peek for filters/pickers, full for forms
33	- **Drag handle:** 36×4px pill, 8px top, `bg-muted`
34	- **Drag-to-dismiss:** velocity ≥ 0.4 or drag > 40% of height
35	- **Backdrop:** `bg-black/40` + `backdrop-blur-sm`
36	- **Height cap:** `max-h-[90dvh]` (dynamic viewport unit = keyboard-safe per iOS 15.4+)
37	- **Rounded top:** `rounded-t-2xl`
38	- **Critical destructive confirms** stay as centered AlertDialog (prevents accidental swipe-dismiss)
39	
40	Applies to: filter panels, new-booking quick-add, client-quick-view, consent form signing prompt, payment-method picker.
41	
42	## 4. FAB placement + safe-area insets
43	
44	Fresha's artist day view has a **bottom-right FAB** (`+`, 56×56) for "new appointment" — the single most-used action. Linear Mobile promoted the "Create Issue" button to a persistent top-of-screen slot in the 2025 redesign (evidence that FAB-only-for-primary is the rule).
45	
46	**InkOS FAB rules:**
47	- One FAB per screen, never two
48	- Primary screens only: Calendar (new booking), Clients (new client), Inventory (new item)
49	- Position: `bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 72px)` (clears bottom nav + 16px), `right: 16px`
50	- Size: 56×56, `rounded-full`, electric-purple bg, `shadow-card` elevated
51	- Tap target stays 56 even if icon is 24
52	- Hides on scroll-down, returns on scroll-up (Fresha pattern)
53	- Respects `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]` on iOS notch devices
54	
55	## 5. Pull-to-refresh
56	
57	**Split call.** iOS Safari standalone PWAs explicitly disable native pull-to-refresh, so we must implement or skip. Linear Mobile (native) has it. Fresha native has it. Cron mobile-web does NOT. Notion mobile-web does NOT. Stripe Dashboard native YES, web NO.
58	
59	**InkOS verdict:** Implement custom PTR only on 3 list screens (Bookings, Clients, Inventory) using `touchstart/touchmove` with `transform: translateY` + a spinner at 60px pull threshold. Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` to prevent double-bounce. Everywhere else, rely on router revalidation. Don't over-ship — PTR on a form or calendar is an antipattern.
60	
61	## 6. Mobile typography scaling
62	
63	Competitor ratios (body text desktop → mobile):
64	- Linear: 14 → 14 (no change, relies on line-height)
65	- Stripe: 14 → 14 (same)
66	- Fresha: 15 → 14
67	- Notion: 16 → 15
68	- Height: 13 → 13 (tight)
69	
70	**InkOS scale:**
71	- h1: 30 → **24** (−20%)
72	- h2: 24 → **20**
73	- h3: 20 → **18**
74	- body: 14 → **14** (unchanged, hold line-height 1.5)
75	- caption: 12 → **12**
76	- Inputs: 16 on mobile (sub-16 triggers iOS auto-zoom — always use 16+)
77	
78	## 7. Touch targets — 44×44 minimum
79	
80	Apple HIG: 44×44pt. Material: 48×48dp. WCAG 2.5.5 AAA: 44×44 CSS px. Common violations audited across the six:
81	- Table row action icons at 24×24 (Notion, Stripe mobile-web — rage-tap territory)
82	- Close "×" buttons at 32×32 (Height, early Linear)
83	- Overflow "⋯" menus shrinking to 28×28 (Cron mobile-web)
84	
85	**InkOS hard gate:** audit every `<button>`, `<a>`, `[role=button]`, form control. Minimum `min-h-11 min-w-11` (44px). Icon-only buttons: `h-11 w-11` with a 20–24px icon centered. Spacing between adjacent targets: 8px min. Sage blocks merge if violated.
86	
87	## 8. Mobile calendar
88	
89	Fresha on 375px defaults to **Day view with agenda list** (not grid) — most practical for artists who only care about "what's next." Swipe horizontal = next/previous day (left=forward, right=back, matches iOS Calendar). Time slots: 30-min rows, current time red line, tap empty slot → bottom sheet "new appointment."
90	
91	Cron mobile keeps time-grid day view (engineer audience). Linear/Stripe/Notion/Height have no calendar.
92	
93	**InkOS calendar:**
94	- `<md` default: Day agenda view. No week-grid ever — unreadable at 375px
95	- Header: `← [Mon Apr 17] →` with current day. Tap date = mini-month picker bottom sheet
96	- Swipe left/right on body = change day (use Framer Motion `dragConstraints`, threshold 80px or velocity 0.3)
97	- Time grid: 60px per 30-min row, current time red 2px line
98	- Tap empty slot → bottom sheet with prefilled time
99	- Tap booking → bottom sheet detail peek (40% snap)
100	- Pinch-zoom deferred to v2
101	
102	## 9. Keyboard avoidance
103	
104	The 2025 winning pattern is **dynamic viewport units + `interactiveWidget: 'resizes-content'`** — no JS observer needed. iOS 15.4+ and all Android Chrome support this.
105	
106	**InkOS form rules:**
107	- Root containers use `min-h-[100dvh]`, never `100vh` (vh doesn't account for keyboard)
108	- Sticky bottom CTA: `bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, position `sticky`, parent has `dvh`
109	- Set `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, interactive-widget=resizes-content">`
110	- On focus, scroll target into view: `input.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center', behavior: 'smooth' })` with 120ms delay (iOS keyboard open time)
111	- Bottom sheets with forms: `max-h-[85dvh]` so keyboard doesn't crop submit button
112	- Known iOS 26 Safari bug: `visualViewport.offsetTop` drifts 0→24px after dismiss — add a 300ms post-blur window scroll-to-top as workaround
113	
114	## 10. Mobile empty states
115	
116	Desktop empty states lecture. Mobile empty states must be scannable in one thumb-glance.
117	
118	**Ratio:** desktop icon 48px → mobile **64px**. Copy desktop 2 sentences → mobile **1 sentence + 1 CTA**. Linear: "No issues. Create your first →". Height: "Nothing here yet" + big `+`. Fresha: illustration + single button.
119	
120	**InkOS pattern per list:**
121	- 64×64 illustration or glyph
122	- One-line headline 16/600
123	- Optional 14/400 subline (max 40 chars)
124	- One primary button, full-width minus 32px margin, `h-12`
125	- Example: "No bookings today" / "Tap + to create one"
126	
127	## 11. Mobile tabs
128	
129	Scrollable + fade-edge is the consensus. Underline > pill for B2B (Linear, Stripe, Notion all underline). Pill fits consumer/ios-native vibe (Fresha customer app).
130	
131	**InkOS:**
132	- Use underline tabs on all report pages and settings sections
133	- Container: `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-hide`, `snap-x snap-mandatory`
134	- Fade edge: `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, black 16px, black calc(100% - 16px), transparent)`
135	- Active tab: 2px bottom border electric-purple, 14/500 text; inactive: 14/400 muted
136	- Min padding per tab: 16px horizontal, 12px vertical (hit-target 44)
137	- Auto-scroll active tab to center on mount
138	
139	Pills reserved for segmented controls (e.g., "Day / Week / Month" toggle) — 2–3 options max.
140	
141	## 12. Mobile search
142	
143	Two patterns:
144	- **Inline:** persistent bar at top — for search-primary screens (Clients, Inventory)
145	- **Icon → full-screen overlay:** for secondary search (Bookings, Reports)
146	
147	Linear uses the icon→overlay pattern. Stripe mobile-web: inline sticky. Fresha clients: inline sticky at top of list. Notion: icon in header → full-screen.
148	
149	**InkOS rule:** Clients and Inventory pages ship inline sticky search (`top-14`, below header, `bg-background/80 backdrop-blur`). Bookings, reports, global nav: icon button → full-screen overlay with recent searches, auto-focus input, Esc/swipe-down to close. Search input always 16px text (no iOS zoom).
150

Whole card tappable → routes to detail page (full screen, not sheet, because of depth). Filter chip tap → bottom sheet with date-range picker + amount range + status multi-select. 1	# InkOS — 12-Sprint Production-Grade UI/UX Hardening Program
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	InkOS has 73 authenticated pages, 13 public pages, 5 admin pages, 31 shadcn primitives, 255 domain components, and 200+ design tokens. Functionally complete, visually inconsistent. The audit surfaced 11 weakness areas: dark mode untested, loading states minimal (only 3 skeletons across 80+ components), error boundaries violate logger contract, mobile calendar broken, empty states ~50% covered, heading weight inconsistent, focus indicators unverified, color contrast unchecked in dark, no page transitions, calendar + consent builder desktop-only, no centralized Logo component.
6	
7	**Goal:** Ship a product that a customer would mistake for Linear, Stripe, or Attio. Every pixel intentional. Every state handled. Every breakpoint graceful. Every interaction < 200ms perceived. Zero console errors in production.
8	
9	**Execution model:** 12 sprints, each 6-10 autonomous hours. Total program: **95-115 hours** of agent work. Runnable in long blocks (5-10 hours per session) with agent coordination and explicit quality gates.
10

12

14	
15	| Pattern | Primary benchmark | Secondary |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| Dashboard + KPI cards | **Linear** home, **Stripe** dashboard | Vercel, Cron |
18	| Calendar | **Cal.com**, **Fantastical** | Google Calendar |
19	| CRM / client profiles | **Attio**, **HubSpot** | Notion databases |
20	| Data tables + filters | **Linear** issues, **Attio** lists | Airtable |
21	| Command palette | **Raycast**, **Linear** cmd+k | Superhuman |
22	| Settings | **Stripe**, **Vercel** | Notion settings |
23	| Empty + loading states | **Linear**, **Height** | Notion |
24	| Motion / transitions | **Linear**, **Arc Browser** | Superhuman |
25	| Public booking (conversion) | **Cal.com** booking, **Calendly** | Stripe Checkout |
26	| Mobile treatment | **Stripe Dashboard mobile**, **Linear mobile** | Cron mobile |

32	## Agent Coordination Model
33	
34	Every sprint follows the **8-agent assembly line**:
35	
36	```
37	1. Nova     — 30-min competitor pass on the target area (screenshots, note patterns)
38	2. Vega     — Produce design spec (tokens, layouts, states, variants, motion)
39	3. Pixel    — For any public-facing page touched this sprint
40	4. Koda     — Build the spec (no design decisions — Vega's spec is law)
41	5. Dato     — Any schema/index/RLS needed for the feature
42	6. Luna     — Visual regression tests (Playwright) + component snapshot tests
43	7. Sage     — Code review gate (a11y, perf, types, security, design compliance)
44	8. Mira     — Capture lessons after each sprint → pattern library
45	```
46	
47	Rex orchestrates; Cadence watches agent performance; Witness classifies every run.
48	
49	**Quality gates** (every sprint must pass all):
50	- `pnpm typecheck` — 0 errors
51	- `pnpm lint --max-warnings=0` — 0 warnings
52	- Playwright visual regression — 0 unexplained diffs in light AND dark
53	- Lighthouse on every touched route — ≥ 90
54	- Axe a11y — 0 serious/critical violations
55	- Bundle size delta — ≤ +5% per sprint
56	- Sage approval — written ship/block verdict
57	
58	Any gate fails → sprint doesn't close → fixes continue until green.

63	
64	**Session pattern:**
65	```
66	Hour 0–1   Nova competitor pass + Vega design spec (parallel)
67	Hour 1–5   Koda implementation (batched, parallel per page)
68	Hour 5–6   Dato + Luna (schema if needed, tests)
69	Hour 6–7   Sage review → fixes
70	Hour 7–8   Visual regression + Lighthouse + a11y gates
71	Hour 8–9   Mira extracts lessons, commits pushed per logical group
72	Hour 9–10  Verification on live Railway deploy
73	```

170	### Sprint 4 — Dark Mode Certification + Theme Toggle (9h)
171	
172	**Theme:** Every pixel verified in both modes. No broken contrast. No invisible text.
173	
174	**Deliverables:**
175	1. **Visual regression pass** — Playwright captures every page in both modes at 1440 and 375px. Diff report lists every contrast/layout issue.
176	2. **Fix contrast issues** — status badges, chart axes/labels, disabled inputs, focus rings, muted text, icons. Audit against WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text + UI).
177	3. **Theme toggle in header** — already in dropdown submenu; add an icon-only `<ThemeToggle>` to the header next to Cmd+K pill. Persists via `next-themes`.

45	
46	  let body: unknown

48	    body = await req.json()
49	  } catch {
50	    return Response.json({ error: 'Invalid JSON' }, { status: 400 })

19	    data: { user },
20	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
21	
22	  if (!user) {
23	    redirect('/login')
24	  }
25	
26	  // Fetch profile, studio membership, and studio in parallel
27	  const [profileResult, memberResult] = await Promise.all([
28	    supabase
29	      .from('profiles')
30	      .select('full_name, avatar_url')
31	      .eq('id', user.id)
32	      .single(),
33	    supabase
34	      .from('studio_members')
35	      .select('role, studio_id, studios(id, name, slug, logo_url, plan_id)')
36	      .eq('user_id', user.id)
37	      .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
38	      .limit(1)
39	      .single(),
40	  ])
41	
42	  const profile = profileResult.data
43	  const member = memberResult.data
44	
45	  if (!member) {
46	    redirect('/onboarding')
47	  }
48	
49	  // M11 FIX: Typed helper derived from the select shape instead of `as` cast.
50	  // The query selects studios(id, name, slug, logo_url) — shape is deterministic.
51	  type JoinedStudio = { id: string; name: string; slug: string; logo_url: string | null }
52	  function isJoinedStudio(v: unknown): v is JoinedStudio {
53	    return (
54	      typeof v === 'object' &&
55	      v !== null &&
56	      'name' in v &&
57	      typeof (v as Record<string, unknown>).name === 'string'
58	    )
59	  }
60	
61	  const studio = isJoinedStudio(member.studios) ? member.studios : null
62	
63	  const studioName = studio?.name ?? 'My Studio'
64	  const studioLogoUrl = studio?.logo_url ?? null
65	  const studioId = member.studio_id
66	  const role = member.role as NavRole
67	
68	  // Subscription / plan
69	  let plan: PlanTier = 'solo'
70	  if (studioId) {
71	    const subResult = await supabase
72	      .from('subscriptions')
73	      .select('plan_tier')
74	      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
75	      .eq('status', 'active')
76	      .maybeSingle()
77	    if (subResult.data?.plan_tier) {
78	      plan = subResult.data.plan_tier as PlanTier
79	    }
80	  }
81	
82	  // Location count (for multi-location nav group)
83	  let locationCount = 0
84	  if (studioId) {
85	    const locResult = await supabase
86	      .from('locations')
87	      .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
88	      .eq('studio_id', studioId)
89	    locationCount = locResult.count ?? 0
90	  }
91	
92	  // Permissions — fetched once here, passed to sidebar + context provider
93	  const permissionsSet =
94	    studioId && user ? await getUserPermissions(studioId, user.id) : new Set<string>()
95	  const permissionKeys = [...permissionsSet]
96	
97	  // Sidebar default-open state from cookie
98	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
99	  const sidebarOpen = cookieStore.get('sidebar_state')?.value !== 'false'
100	
101	  const userName = profile?.full_name ?? user.email?.split('@')[0] ?? 'You'
102	  const userEmail = user.email ?? ''
103	  const userAvatarUrl = profile?.avatar_url ?? null
104	
105	  // Compute filtered navGroups for MobileNav (same logic as AppSidebar)
106	  const permissions = new Set(permissionKeys)
107	  const navGroups = APP_NAV
108	    .filter((group) => !(group.condition === 'multi-location' && locationCount <= 1))
109	    .map((group) => ({
110	      ...group,
111	      items: group.items.filter((item) => {
112	        if (!item.requiredRoles.includes(role)) return false
113	        if (item.requiredPermission && !permissions.has(item.requiredPermission)) return false
114	        return true
115	      }),
116	    }))
117	    .filter((group) => group.items.length > 0)
118	
119	  return (
120	    <PermissionsProvider permissionKeys={permissionKeys}>
121	      <SidebarProvider defaultOpen={sidebarOpen} className="h-svh">
122	        <AppSidebar
123	          locationCount={locationCount}
124	          plan={plan}
125	          studioName={studioName}
126	          studioLogoUrl={studioLogoUrl}
127	          role={role}
128	          permissionKeys={permissionKeys}
129	        />
130	        <AppHeader
131	          studioName={studioName}
132	          userName={userName}
133	          userEmail={userEmail}
134	          userAvatarUrl={userAvatarUrl}
135	          navGroups={navGroups}
136	        >
137	          {children}
138	        </AppHeader>
139	      </SidebarProvider>
140	    </PermissionsProvider>
141	  )
142	}
